summary: RP1 Spatial Fabric is the idea that a place in three dimensions can be a document with a URL, the way a web page is, plus the stack that makes that real: a signed fabric file, a native engine that reads it, and a browser that opens it. The fabric file is a compact JSON Web Signature over a JSON manifest, signed RS256 against an X.509 chain carried in the header, listing WebAssembly modules that may be pinned by hash and a scene tree of packed 528-byte node records with 64-bit positions; a portal is simply a node with subtype 255 whose resource reference is the URL of another fabric, so fabrics nest and each nested one is verified on its own. Correction, dated 2026-09-03: this record previously said the browser had no public source and that two engine dependencies were private, which was true when it was observed on 2026-08-13 and is not true now; since 2026-09-01 the engine Sneeze, the browser Rubidium, the realtime library RMAP, the map library Map and the guest SDK are all public repositories, and the engine's dependency manifest clones the two former blockers from public addresses. Read the licences before reusing any of it: the engine, the SDK and RMAP are Apache-2.0, the browser's own README calls it proprietary with all rights reserved, and Map ships no licence file. The trap is smaller than it was but still the main one: there is now a published interface header the vendor calls the canonical frozen contract, but there is still no fabric-file specification and no conformance suite, so compatible with this format has no testable meaning, and three incompatible manifest dialects still ship together inside one public repository at one commit, including a signed sample whose payload disagrees with the unsigned source file beside it. Signing works and is stable, but signature acceptance is not scene compatibility, and the vendor's own documentation records that the browser currently pins the trust level instead of acting on the one it computed.

coverage.note: The fabric file is the container: a compact JSON Web Signature whose payload holds the serialized manifest under a data claim, with members for container name, declared services and a module list of url and hash pairs, and the scene tree under Data.Scene. The public sample fabric in the engine repository is exactly that, and the browser signs and verifies these files from its own command line.
